paper.title: Two-dimensional Penning ionization electron spectroscopy of CO/He*(2^3S)
paper.journal: Journal of Electron Spectroscopy and Related Phenomena

research.topic: Two-dimensional Penning ionization electron spectroscopy (2D-PIES) of CO by collision with He*(2^3S)
objectives: Observe collision energy dependence of partial ionization cross-sections (CEDPICS) for CO/He*(2^3S)
Reproduce CEDPICS theoretically using classical trajectory calculations with anisotropic potential energy surfaces
Calculate potential energy surfaces for entrance and exit channels (ionic ground and excited states of CO+–He)
Generate collision-energy-resolved PIES (CERPIES) and convert to 2D-PIES for comparison with experiment
methods: Experimental 2D-PIES with time-of-flight and hemispherical electron analyzer
Classical trajectory calculations on entrance potential energy surface
Ab initio molecular orbital calculations for potential energy surfaces: CCSD(T)/6-311+G* for entrance (Li–CO model), MRSDCI, OVGF, HF for exit channels
Ionization width based on electron exchange mechanism

ionic_states.label: A
ionic_states.description: First excited ionic state of CO+

ionic_states.label: B
ionic_states.description: Second excited ionic state of CO+

theory.framework: Classical trajectory calculations with ionization probability on anisotropic potential energy surfaces

entrance_potential.method: CCSD(T)/6-311+G* with full counterpoise correction for basis set superposition error
entrance_potential.model: Li–CO potential energy surface V_0(R,θ) scaled by factor 0.55 to mimic He*(2^3S)–CO
entrance_potential.coordinates: R = distance between Li/He and center of mass of CO, θ = angle between C–X–Li/He

methods: MRSDCI (multi-reference single and double excitation configuration interaction) with MIDI-4 polarization basis
exit_potentials.description: Exit potentials V_i(R,θ) for He–CO+ (ionic states X, A, B). MRSDCI directly calculates V_i; OVGF and HF compute neutral He–CO ground state interaction V_0 plus ionization potentials IP_i(R,θ). Absolute values corrected by observed IPs at infinite separation.

ionization_width.approximation: One-electron approximation, spin inversion for He*(2^3S) eliminates first term, anisotropic dependence governed by compact 1s and ionized orbitals
ionization_width.constants: K_i ratios: K_X : K_A : K_B = 1.00 : 3.06 : 1.41 (determined to reproduce observed branching ratios and collision energy dependence)

trajectory_calculation.details: 3000 trajectories per collision energy, impact parameter b = 0–7 Å, initial vibrational/rotational energies of CO from Boltzmann distribution at 300 K, partial ionization cross-section σ_i = 2π ∫ b P_i db
trajectory_calculation.electron_energy: E_e = V_0(R,θ) - V_i(R,θ) at each trajectory step
trajectory_calculation.CERPIES: Sum of electron transition probabilities for specific electron kinetic energies at each step
trajectory_calculation.vibrational_structure: Distributed according to Franck-Condon factors from UPS data of CO

numerical.energy_resolution: ~80 meV (fwhm of Ar 2P_{3/2} peak in He I UPS)

observables.2D-PIES: Intensity as function of electron kinetic energy (E_e) and collision energy (E_c) or TOF
observables.CERPIES: Collision-energy-resolved PIES (electron energy spectra at specific collision energies)
observables.CEDPICS: Collision-energy dependence of partial ionization cross-sections for X, A, B states (log σ_i vs log E_c)
observables.partial_ionization_cross_sections: σ_i(E_c) for i = X, A, B
observables.total_ionization_cross_section: σ_total(E_c) (normalized to σ|9Å at E_c=100 meV from Ref. [19])
observables.bandwidth_broadening_DW: Change in peak width (fwhm) with collision energy
observables.peak_energy_shift_DE: Shift in peak position with collision energy
observables.units: Cross-sections in cm^2 (or relative units), energies in meV

results.experimental_2D-PIES: Contour map shows distinct bands for X, A, B states; CERPIES at E_c≈100 meV and 250 meV show peak shifts and broadening
results.CEDPICS: Positive slope in log–log plot for all states; steepest for A state, indicating soft repulsive potential for side-on collisions at higher energies
results.entrance_potential_scaling: Scaling Li–CO potential by 0.55 reproduces CEDPICS slope; CEDPICS independent of exit potential choice

calculated_2D-PIES.MRSDCI: Best agreement with experiment; DE_B = 44 meV close to experimental 64 meV; DW_B = 25 meV vs experimental 16 meV
calculated_2D-PIES.OVGF: Reasonable but underestimates DE_B (30 meV) due to weak attractive interaction in B state
calculated_2D-PIES.HF: Overestimates B state bandwidth broadening (DW_B = 31 meV) due to deep potential well around oxygen end; DE_B = 31 meV

results.discrepancy_X_state: Calculated X state intensity increases with collision energy while experiment stays constant; attributed to insufficient electron correlation in entrance potential (less steep would reduce slope)
results.conclusion: MRSDCI exit potentials give best agreement; HF overestimates B state well; OVGF reasonable but less accurate for B state; entrance potential needs better correlation treatment

Fig_1.description: (a) Observed 2D-PIES of CO/He*(2^3S) with contour map (arbitrary linear scale) and CERPIES at E_c≈100 meV (solid) and 250 meV (dotted). (b) CEDPICS: experimental circles, calculated solid curves; double circle is total ionization cross-section from Ref. [19] at 100 meV.

Fig_2.description: Calculated entrance and exit potential energy curves V_0(R,θ) and V_i(R,θ) in meV. Contour maps for entrance and exit (MRSDCI) with lines every 100 meV. Exit curves for X, A, B states from MRSDCI (solid), OVGF (dashed), HF (chained). Negative contours for B state shown as dashed (-200, -100 meV).

Fig_3.description: Calculated 2D-PIES using exit potentials from (a) MRSDCI, (b) OVGF, (c) HF. Right panels show CERPIES at E_c=100 meV (solid) and 250 meV (dotted).

equations.Eq_1: A* + M → A + M_i^+ + e^- (Penning ionization)
equations.Eq_3: σ(E_e, v_r) = C I(E_e, v_r) / I_He*(v_r) * (v_r/v_He*) (cross-section from TOF data)
equations.Eq_5: Γ_i = 2π ρ_el ⟨F_i| H_el | F_0⟩ (ionization width, Fermi's golden rule)
equations.Eq_6: ⟨F_i| H_el | F_0⟩ ≈ ∑_K [c_{2s}(1) f_i(2) - c_{2s}(2) f_i(1)] / r_{12} (one-electron approximation)
equations.Eq_7: Γ_i ≈ 2C ⟨f_i| c_{1s}⟩ (approximation with average constant C)
equations.Eq_8: Γ_i = K_i ⟨f_i| c_{1s}⟩ (final form with state-specific constant K_i)
equations.Eq_9: σ_i = 2π ∫_0^∞ b P_i db (partial ionization cross-section from trajectories)

limitations.entrance_potential: Li–CO model potential scaled by 0.55; insufficient electron correlation leads to discrepancy in X state CEDPICS slope
limitations.classical_trajectory: No quantum effects (tunneling, interference); fixed CO internuclear distance (no vibration during collision)
limitations.exit_potentials: HF method overestimates attractive well for B state; OVGF underestimates attraction; MRSDCI most accurate but computationally expensive
limitations.ionization_width: Approximated by overlap of 1s and ionized orbitals; constant K_i fitted to experiment, not ab initio
limitations.vibrational_structure: Franck-Condon factors from UPS, not calculated for each geometry
